item.title: Go Daily Question 146
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "time"
)

func main() {
    t := struct {
        time.Time
        N int
    }{
        time.Date(2020, 12, 20, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC),
        5,
    }

    m, _ := json.Marshal(t)
    fmt.Printf("%s", m)
}
  • A: {“Time”: “2020-12-20T00:00:00Z”, “N”: 5 };
  • B: “2020-12-20T00:00:00Z”;
  • C: {“N”: 5};
  • D: <nil>
🔑 Answer Analysis:

B Run online

In Go, structs can embed anonymous structs, thereby achieving effects similar to inheritance. For example, the following struct embeds the anonymous struct time.Time:

item.title: Go Daily Question 135
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
)

type AutoGenerated struct {
    Age   int    `json:"age"`
    Name  string `json:"name"`
    Child []int  `json:"child"`
}

func main() {
    jsonStr1 := `{"age": 14,"name": "potter", "child":[1,2,3]}`
    a := AutoGenerated{}
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonStr1), &a)
    aa := a.Child
    fmt.Println(aa)
    jsonStr2 := `{"age": 12,"name": "potter", "child":[3,4,5,7,8,9]}`
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonStr2), &a)
    fmt.Println(aa)
}
  • A: [1 2 3] [1 2 3];
  • B: [1 2 3] [3 4 5];
  • C: [1 2 3] [3 4 5 6 7 8 9];
  • D: [1 2 3] [3 4 5 0 0 0]
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B Run online

item.title: Go Daily Question 124
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "time"
)

func main() {
    t := struct {
        time.Time
        N int
    }{
        time.Date(2020, 12, 20, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC),
        5,
    }

    m, _ := json.Marshal(t)
    fmt.Printf("%s", m)
}

A: {“Time”: “2020-12-20T00:00:00Z”, “N”: 5 }; B: “2020-12-20T00:00:00Z”; C: {“N”: 5}; D: <nil>

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B In the problem, time.Time is embedded in the anonymous struct, which means it inherits time.Time. time.Time overrides the MarshalJSON method, so it will output according to the format specified by time.Time’s MarshalJSON.

item.title: Go Daily Question 043
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
)

type AutoGenerated struct {
    Age   int    `json:"age"`
    Name  string `json:"name"`
    Child []int  `json:"child"`
}

func main() {
    jsonStr1 := `{"age": 14,"name": "potter", "child":[1,2,3]}`
    a := AutoGenerated{}
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonStr1), &a)
    aa := a.Child
    fmt.Println(aa)
    jsonStr2 := `{"age": 12,"name": "potter", "child":[3,4,5,7,8,9]}`
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonStr2), &a)
    fmt.Println(aa)
}
  • A：[1 2 3] [1 2 3]
  • B：[1 2 3] [3 4 5]
  • C：[1 2 3] [3 4 5 6 7 8 9]
  • D：[1 2 3] [3 4 5 0 0 0]
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B Analysis: When JSON deserializes, slices are handled by setting the slice’s len to 0 and then appending data. Because aa := a.Child, both aa and a.Child slices point to the same array. When appending to 6, since a.Child had not yet expanded, modifying the underlying array was equivalent to modifying aa’s data. However, when appending to 7, the a.Child slice expanded and pointed to a new array. Therefore, the data of aa is [3 4 5].
